title: 正文可点词标注·待接入 v1.1（义项修订）
status: 待接入设计稿的义项修订，不是已经上线的页面，不代表网站已更新或已修复
provenance: 根据已审定的场景稿 v1.1、阅读稿 v2.1、独立背词与复习稿 v1.1 的英文原文标注可点范围。本包在 anchors v1 上修订了 last 的错挂，并去掉重复的 wait 句。标注本身是学习产品数据，不是真实聊天记录。

offsetSpec.noteZh: start 和 end 是对应 textEn 的 Unicode 码位下标，左闭右开；surface 必须等于 textEn[start:end]。本包全部字符都在基本多文种平面，因此在 JavaScript 里用 str.slice(start, end) 也一致。原文若改了，必须重算，不要手改下标。

integrationNotes: 这是 content-text-anchors-v1.1，在 v1 上修订了两处数据，不是重新生成全部标注。不是已经上线的页面，不代表网站已更新或已修复，也未改网站源码。
正文仍以各包 JSON 为准。复习句以 independent-vocab-review-pack-v1.1 为源。不要重跑 build-content-text-anchors-v1.py 来生成或覆盖本文件：该脚本只写 content-text-anchors-v1.json，且会按 encounter 级目标标注，使 last weekend 再次错挂。
场景只标注该场的本课词卡（含可选卡）。阅读标注本包词卡，同一词在另一篇里复现也可点，仍打开同一张卡。复习必须按该句的 sentences[].targetCardIds 标注；不能再用 encounter 级合集去标全部句子。
点开后的词卡交互仍按独立背词稿：先揭释义，再按需展开例句和说明。查看中文、释义、例句或答案不记为掌握。
中文仍按句或按段按需展开，不要在每一行固定放一个中文按钮。可点词是正文里的轻标记，不是句末按钮。
阅读稿里 hold on to、manage to 有意不出现在正文，本包不为它们标正文范围；它们仍可作为见过卡留在读后说明。
场景稿开场 I'm already in the game 仍可能被读成已经在打一局。这是原文可选润色，本包不改那一句。
目录权限恢复后，由开发负责人把本包和词卡翻面一并接入；本稿不能证明网站已更新。

intentionallyUnanchored.reasonZh: 阅读稿 v2.1 已把骑车段正文改成 hold her，本卡只作为见过、不强制先背，保留在读后说明里。正文没有 hold on to，因此不标可点范围。
阅读稿 v2.1 正文写的是 rode past，本卡只作为见过、不强制先背，保留在读后说明里。正文没有 manage to，因此不标可点范围。

units.textEn: You free tonight? I'm already in the game.
Give me ten minutes? I'm just finishing something.
No rush. I'll wait for you.
Okay, I'm here. Did you send me an invite?
Yeah, a minute ago. You don't see it?
Not yet. Can you send it again?
Sent. It should be there now.
Got it. Wait — it says I can't get in.
That's weird. Try again? It does that sometimes.
Okay, I'm in your party now.
I would, but it's getting late. I have to get up early tomorrow.
Yeah. I'll message you when I'm free.
Okay. I'll wait for you next time.
I just sent you a link. Can you open it?
The page won't load. It just keeps spinning.
That's weird. It works on my phone.
Did you try refreshing the page?
I don't think so. Everything else is fine. Let me try restarting my browser.
I restarted the browser and signed in again. I can see the page now.
All good. What did you want me to look at?
The time on the first page. Does it look right to you?
Almost — it says three, but we said three thirty.
Oh. I'll fix that. Thanks for catching it.
No problem. I'll stay on the page if you want me to check again.
That'd be great. Give me a minute.

At half past twelve on Saturday, I left home with a short shopping list: bread, milk, and dish soap. I planned to buy everything at the supermarket and come straight back. Outside the entrance, I met my neighbor, Anna.
She was looking at the bent handle of her umbrella. It got caught in a bus door the day before. She wanted a stronger one from a shop near the station, but the shop was closed until two.

“I'm going to have lunch while I wait,” she said. “Have you eaten?”

I hadn't. My shopping could wait, and I hadn't bought anything yet, so we went to a café together.

We found a table at the back, away from the coffee machine. Anna ordered soup. I chose a cheese sandwich, then wished I'd ordered the soup when hers arrived with warm bread. She pushed the bread basket between us.

Over lunch, we talked about our building. Someone had put plants beside the front door, making the entrance feel less empty. Anna knew who it was. We also talked about the upstairs washing machine, which always seemed to start just as she went to bed.

At two, we walked to the umbrella shop. She opened both, and I stood with her under each one to see how much they covered. The wider one covered us both, but she said she didn't want to carry something that large every day. She chose the smaller one.

Neither of us was in a hurry. The river was only a few streets away, so we walked there and sat on a bench. A man was teaching his daughter to ride a bike. Each time he let go, she shouted for him to hold her again. We stayed until she rode past our bench on her own.

It was after three when I finally returned to the supermarket. I bought everything on my list, picking up the milk last. Back home, I put it straight in the fridge. My quick shopping trip had filled most of the afternoon.
On Sunday, Ben was coming to my apartment for lunch at twelve thirty. We planned to eat pasta and then watch a movie. At twelve, I had chopped the vegetables, but I hadn't started cooking.
Five minutes later, he sent a message. His bus had broken down, and he was waiting for another one. He thought he could arrive at about one fifteen.
I was already hungry. For a moment, I thought about eating without him. Instead, I had some toast and put the vegetables in the fridge. I messaged him: "No rush. Just tell me when you're nearby."
At one, his next message arrived. He was ten minutes away. I started the sauce and put a pan of water on the stove.

Ben arrived carrying a small bag of tomatoes from his garden. While the pasta cooked, he cut them for a salad. We ate at half past one. The movie started later than planned, but we still had time to finish it before he went home.
I'm going to wear a jacket.
I wear these shoes at home.
Put the bowls on the table.
Put the keys in the bag.
I still need to clean the kitchen.
Can you bring me my phone?
Can you take a look at this?
The stove is on. Turn it off.
The last bus is at ten.
If we walk now, we can catch it.
Yeah. Give me a minute to change.
I am, but I'm a bit tired. I need to go to bed early.
My neighbor sent me a message.
I'll reply later. I'm still on the bus.
If we leave now, we can still be on time.
I don't want to miss the bus.
Do you want to cook tonight?
I'll bring them. I won't forget.
I'm going to wear a jacket.
Can you take a look at this email?
There's some rice in the fridge. We can eat that.
Yeah. I need to get up early tomorrow.
